program_plain: World: 400 self-propelled agents moving in a wrap-around 20x20 square. Rules each step: each agent takes the average heading of agents within distance 1, adds heading noise of up to 0.1 rad, and moves at speed 0.3.
model_family: active matter / dry polar flocking (Vicsek model, periodic box)
standard_name: Vicsek model (scalar-noise, metric alignment); low-noise macrocluster / traveling-band clustering; vortex/milling state in Vicsek-like variants
citations: Vicsek et al 1995, PRL 75:1226 - original model (title from reference list)

Chaté, Ginelli, Grégoire, Raynaud 2008, PRE 77:046113 - comprehensive study of Vicsek-style models
Solon, Chaté, Tailleur 2015, PRL 114:068101 - liquid-gas transition, micro-phase separation into traveling bands
Barberis 2018, PRE 98:032607 - single macrocluster in the Vicsek model at very low noise
Czirók & Vicsek 2000, Physica A 281:17-29 - rotation/vortex at high density, low noise in bounded domains
Costanzo & Hemelrijk 2018 (venue unverified), spontaneous milling in a Vicsek-like model - needs reduced field of view and max turning rate; not in plain alignment-only Vicsek
Vicsek & Zafeiris 2012, Phys. Rep. 517:71 - review (seen only in a reference list, not read)
searches: Vicsek model low noise milling vortex clusters without attraction
Vicsek model collective motion first-order transition traveling bands Chaté 2008
Vicsek model small noise large speed disordered clusters vortices lattice-like cluster phase
Czirók Vicsek Collective behavior of interacting self-propelled particles Physica A 2000 rotating vortex
Vicsek alignment-only periodic boundary stable vortex or rotating clusters dense bands microphase separation Solon Chaté Tailleur
notes: Clumping is well documented for the Vicsek model. Milling is documented only for bounded domains or for variants with limited field of view. Low polar order at rho=1, v0=0.3, noise 0.1 contradicts the standard expectation of a polar liquid or macrocluster. This suggests a metric artifact, an implementation quirk (e.g. angle averaging) or baseline-relative scoring. Check the implementation before treating this as novel. The Costanzo & Hemelrijk venue and year were not confirmed by the search, and I did not read the Vicsek & Zafeiris review.
full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN-VARIANT (confidence: low-to-medium).** The model and two of the three observed features are well documented. The combination of strong milling with low polar order is not something I found described for this exact periodic, alignment-only system.

**1. Model family.** This is active matter, specifically dry polar active matter. The rules are the standard Vicsek model: constant-speed particles, local average-heading alignment, scalar noise, periodic box. The Vicsek model has constant-speed self-propelled particles that interact only via local alignment of their velocities in a noisy environment. The parameters here are density ρ = 400/400 = 1, interaction radius 1, v₀ = 0.3 and noise up to 0.1 rad. That is very low noise, deep in the nominally ordered phase. The 800-agent variant has ρ = 2 and sits even deeper in it.

**2. Specific behaviour: what the literature says.**
- **Clumping (nn ratio 0.2): KNOWN.**
  - Grégoire & Chaté found that the 2D transition is always discontinuous, including for the minimal Vicsek model.
  - Solon, Chaté & Tailleur showed that the flocking transition is best understood as a liquid-gas transition. It involves micro-phase separation into a smectic arrangement of traveling ordered bands.
  - At very low noise, Barberis (PRE 98, 032607) reports a macrocluster containing a macroscopic fraction of the particles. This is the closest match to heavy clumping at η = 0.1.
- **Milling or vortex motion: KNOWN-VARIANT.**
  - Czirók & Vicsek report that rotation develops in the high-density, low-noise regime. That rotation appears when the Vicsek model is simulated in a bounded domain. The same bounded-domain result is described in the "Swarming in bounded domains" paper. It does not appear in periodic boundaries.
  - Costanzo & Hemelrijk say milling has been reproduced in more complex models but not in simpler alignment-only models like the Vicsek model. They find it needs both a reduced field of view and a reduced maximal angular velocity.
  - I found no source reporting stable milling in the plain periodic-box Vicsek model.
- **Low polar order (−2.0): this conflicts with expectation.** The standard result at these parameters is high polarisation, with a polar liquid or a single big cluster. A low-polarity state with strong milling therefore does not follow from the standard model.

**3. Citations checked against search results.**
- Vicsek, Czirók, Ben-Jacob, Cohen, Shochet 1995, PRL 75, 1226, "Novel type of phase transition in a system of self-driven particles". This is the original model. Title, venue and year come from a reference list, not the paper itself.
- Grégoire & Chaté 2004, PRL 92, 025702, "Onset of collective and cohesive motion". Verified on arXiv.
- Chaté, Ginelli, Grégoire, Raynaud 2008, PRE 77, 046113, "Collective motion of self-propelled particles interacting without cohesion". Verified on PubMed and the Aberdeen portal.
- Solon, Chaté, Tailleur 2015, PRL 114, 068101. Verified on arXiv 1406.6088.
- Czirók & Vicsek 2000, Physica A 281, 17–29, "Collective behavior of interacting self-propelled particles". Verified on ScienceDirect.
- Barberis 2018, PRE 98, 032607. Verified on APS.
- Costanzo & Hemelrijk, "Spontaneous emergence of milling (vortex state) in a Vicsek-like model". The title is verified, but the venue and year (J. Phys. D, 2018) are from memory and not confirmed by the search.
- Vicsek & Zafeiris 2012, Phys. Rep. 517, 71, "Collective motion". This is the standard review. It appears in a reference list, and I did not read it.

**4. Caveats.**
- The milling and polar scores may come from how the simulator or metric works. Examples are angle-averaging instead of vector-averaging, a milling metric that picks up local swirl inside a clump, or scores measured relative to a baseline. A high-density clump with a rotating core would be consistent with the Barberis macrocluster plus the bounded-domain vortices. Check the implementation before treating this as a new phenomenon.
- The "milling" in this system is probably a different object from the vortices and mills seen in models with attraction or limited vision.

3. Vicsek model small noise large speed disordered clusters vortices lattice-like cluster phase

5. Vicsek alignment-only periodic boundary stable vortex or rotating clusters dense bands microphase separation Solon Chaté Tailleur
